open: A locked-off shot from a scripted feature film, a slow dark drama with made-up characters played by actors on a closed set. One continuous shot with no cuts. No camera movement.

clips.full: A shot from a scripted feature film with made-up characters played by actors on a closed set, filmed hand-held from the ground like news footage. One continuous shot with no cuts. The camera stays where it is and is only very slightly unsteady. The two placards sway slightly on their sticks, out of time with each other, and the lettering on them stays exactly as it is. The flare on the cobbles burns and its smoke leans to the left and thickens. The hoods and hats shift a little. The steel barrier does not move. Nobody speaks a word that can be made out. Sound: a flare hissing, a large crowd murmuring with no words in it, a steel barrier rattling once. No music. No dialogue. Thanks.

clips.text: For the first three seconds nothing moves except the smoke outside the window, slowly, and the table lamp, which flickers once. Then the man at the window raises the remote control slowly to chest height, pointed at the glass, and presses one button. When he presses it, the glow outside the window swells brighter and redder for a moment and settles. Then he holds perfectly still. The curtains and the telephone do not move. Sound: a low electrical hum, one plastic click, and a muffled crowd roar through glass with no words in it. No dialogue.

clips.full: A shot from a scripted feature film with made-up characters played by actors on a closed set, filmed hand-held from the ground like news footage. One continuous shot with no cuts. The camera stays where it is and is only very slightly unsteady. The two men on the crates keep pointing across the street at each other, arms straight. Both men shout the same words at the same moment through their megaphones. They say: And I'll tell you whose fault it is. The voices are harsh and distorted and echo off the buildings. Then both hold the point, perfectly still, glaring. The flare on the cobbles burns and its smoke drifts across the bottom of the frame. The crowds behind the barriers stand still and the flags stir. The only sounds are the two megaphone voices, a flare hissing and the wind. No music. Thanks.

A shot from a scripted feature film with made-up characters played by actors on a closed set, filmed hand-held from the ground like news footage. One continuous shot with no cuts. The camera stays where it is and is only very slightly unsteady. Pink smoke drifts slowly across the columns from left to right and thins. The flare light flickers on the stone. The tips of the flags stir. The carved word on the building stays exactly as it is. The placard in the puddle does not move. Sound: a far-off crowd roar with no words in it, a flare hissing, water dripping. No music. No dialogue. Thanks.

A shot from a scripted feature film with made-up characters played by actors on a closed set, filmed hand-held from the ground like news footage. One continuous shot with no cuts. The camera stays where it is and is only very slightly unsteady. The man in the long overcoat takes three slow steps toward the camera and stops, looking ahead past the lens. The man behind his shoulder follows and stops too, chewing. Behind them the pallet truck is hauled a little way forward and stops. The yellow jacket in the foreground does not move. The crowds keep their backs turned, the flags stir and flare smoke drifts across the strip. Nobody speaks. Sound: slow footsteps on wet cobbles, small steel wheels grinding, a flare hissing and a far-off crowd with no words in it. No music. No dialogue. Thanks.

A shot from a scripted feature film with made-up characters played by actors on a closed set, filmed on a cheap camcorder with its own light. One continuous shot with no cuts. The camera is hand-held and shakes slightly but stays where it is. The two men in front keep tipping their pints back, swallowing, with beer running down their chins. The man on the left finishes first, bangs his empty glass down on the bar and roars with both arms up. The other is still drinking. Behind them the man on the stool takes one very small sip from his little glass and his face does not change at all. Sound: gulping, a glass banging down on wood, one wordless roar and laughter off camera. Nobody says a word that can be made out. No music. Thanks.

A shot from a scripted feature film with made-up characters played by actors on a closed set, filmed on a cheap camcorder with its own light. One continuous shot with no cuts. The camera is hand-held and shakes slightly but stays where it is. The man at the throwing line sways, squints and throws the dart. It flies wide and sticks in the wood panelling beside the dartboard in the foreground. He throws both arms up in triumph anyway and nearly falls over. The man crouching behind the armchair flinches and keeps chewing. The darts already in the wall do not move. Sound: a dart thudding into wood, one man cheering with no words and laughter off camera. Nobody says a word that can be made out. No music. Thanks.

A shot from a scripted feature film with made-up characters played by actors on a closed set, filmed on a cheap camcorder with its own light. One continuous shot with no cuts. The camera is hand-held and shakes slightly but stays where it is. The man lying across the pool table jabs the cue from behind his back and misses the ball completely, and the cue skids across the cloth. He wheezes with laughter, eyes shut, and lets his forehead drop onto the table. The man in the armchair behind him slowly shakes his head without lifting his face from his hand. The two balls near the lens do not move. Sound: a cue scraping on cloth, a man wheezing with laughter and a glass rolling on wood. Nobody says a word that can be made out. No music. Thanks.

A shot from a scripted feature film with made-up characters played by actors on a closed set, filmed on a cheap camcorder with its own light. One continuous shot with no cuts. The camera is hand-held and shakes slightly but stays where it is. The kneeling man heaves twice into the bucket, his shoulders jerking, and then stays down, breathing hard. The hand keeps patting his back in a slow steady rhythm. The old man in the chair stares straight ahead and does not react at all, then blinks once. Sound: a man retching into a metal bucket, a hand patting cloth, far-off party chatter with no words in it and canvas flapping in the wind. Nobody says a word that can be made out. No music. Thanks.

clips.text: The man between the two newspapers looks from one newspaper to the other and back. He says: Hang on. Which one's true? He speaks slowly and suspiciously, with a pause after the first two words. Then he holds still, frowning. The face on the laptop beside him does not react. The only sounds are his voice, a bare bulb buzzing and rain on a metal roof.

The man between the two newspapers keeps frowning at them and does not speak. The face on the laptop screen says: Doesn't matter. I don't need them to believe it. I need them to reply. He speaks in a flat quiet monotone, slightly bored, through a small laptop speaker, and does not blink. Then nobody moves. The only sounds are that voice through the laptop, a bare bulb buzzing and rain on a metal roof.

The three men hold their poses with their arms straight and do not move their feet. The red light sweeps round the corridor again and again. Mr Blue, the man at the left, shouts: Who talked? Mr Red, the man at the right, shouts: He talked. Mr Blue shouts: Your lot always talk. The man in the middle keeps his arms spread and keeps smiling. The only sounds are their two voices and a loud bell ringing close by.
clips.note: second wording: the first named the pistols and "aim" and was refused twice as a possible policy violation

clips.text: Nobody speaks. The two men at the sides hold their poses, perfectly still, breathing hard. The man in the middle keeps his arms spread and turns his head slowly from one to the other and back, smiling. The red light sweeps round the corridor again and again. The things on the floor do not move. Sound: a loud bell ringing close by. No dialogue.

The woman stands completely still with her back to the camera, looking across the road. Rain falls hard through the lamp light and bounces on the road. The carrier bag in her hand swings very slightly. The lettering on the board stays exactly as it is. The street lamp flickers once. Sound: heavy rain on a pavement, a street lamp buzzing and water running in a gutter. No dialogue.

clips.full: A shot from a scripted feature film, a slow dark drama with a made-up character played by an actor on a closed set. One continuous shot with no cuts. For the first two seconds the woman looks straight ahead and does not move while rain runs down her face. Then she slowly tips her head back until she is looking straight up into the rain, and closes her eyes. When her eyes close, the camera tilts slowly upward, letting her face leave the bottom of the frame, until the frame holds only black sky with rain falling toward the lens through orange lamp light. Then it holds still. Sound: heavy rain and one slow breath out. No music. No dialogue. Thanks.

clips.text: The bunch of keys in the foreground swings slowly from the finger and the paper tags turn. Steam moves on the inside of the café window and the strip light flickers once. Fine rain falls. The lettering on the board stays exactly as it is. The shutter, the bicycle and the bin bags do not move. Sound: keys clinking, light rain and a far-off bus. No dialogue.
